Competing near-zero radial configurations yield the cutoff min(d+alpha,md), including logarithmic boundary divergence, while moment finiteness is by inductive projection bounds. The backward affine series converges by strict average projection contraction, has every subcritical moment, and coupling proves unique stationarity. Dirichlet size bias gives exact squared-norm inverse moments, and the recursion yields stationary mean-square risk. The supplied checker reproduces 70 finite diagnostic conditions, but no infinite step relies on finite computation.

value.rationale: A full sharp integrability spectrum supplies the exact noise-amplification boundary for a natural fresh-data randomized row projection solver. It reveals the genuine interaction of number of candidates m, geometric dimension d, and importance exponent alpha: even maximal bias cannot suppress the event all m Gaussian rows nearly vanish. The explicit alpha=2 stationary variance quantifies physical quadratic error risk and distinguishes geometric coupling from mean-square stability. This is more than a parameter rename of fixed-data RK; the independently noisy affine data introduce a singular radial mechanism and a stationary-law problem absent from the main sources.
